decisions.reason: Even after two years without visible website support, its flagship status, fit with the stated cloud messaging direction, and the firm's sunk development and reputational commitment make management more likely to persist than to formally withdraw it.

It had meaningful initial commitment through its own page, but after several years with no visible market presence and only an adjacent fit to the core messaging strategy, management can now more easily justify ending it and reallocating resources.

Because it was only lightly promoted, is less central to the firm's forward-looking cloud innovation story, and has been absent from view for years, escalation forces are now too weak to prevent withdrawal.

As a narrow feature with low public commitment and prolonged non-observation, it is the easiest offer for management to discontinue once continued weak relevance can no longer be blamed on temporary launch conditions.

Security remains tightly linked to the firm's secure and compliant positioning, so despite reduced visibility management is still inclined to retain this offer or keep it embedded rather than remove it outright.

Although it supports the secure email proposition, its modest standalone visibility and the long gap since any observable promotion mean management is now slightly more likely to rationalize the portfolio and drop it.
